target.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running browser screenshot with a configured image-understanding model would have the session become unusable when that vision model failed: later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` tool results were framed as image analysis until `/new`.

The vision-failure path previously fell back to injecting a raw base64 image block into the tool result. That image-bearing result is retained across recent completed turns, so it keeps re-entering model context and contaminates subsequent tool use.

This is the failure path described in #106703 (and the same root cause reported in #105305).

## Why This Change Was Made

The vision success path already returns a text-only description. This change makes the configured-vision failure path consistent with it: on describe failure, return a text-only result that reports the failure reason and keeps the staged outbound-copy path so the screenshot can still be shared explicitly via the message tool. Never write base64 image data into session/tool-result state on that path.

Scoped intentionally:

- Configured vision model throws → text-only (fixed path). A user who configured image understanding opted into text descriptions, so a transient provider error should not silently switch to dumping raw base64.
- Image understanding skipped / not configured (`describeBrowserScreenshot` returns `null`) → still returns the raw image, so vision-capable primary models that rely on seeing the screenshot are unaffected.

## User Impact

When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the session stays usable: tool results remain text-framed, and the screenshot can still be shared via the message tool. Users without image understanding configured keep the previous model-visible screenshot behavior.

## Evidence

### Behavior repro against the real session-state code

The reported symptom is a session-state effect: the vision-failure screenshot result persists across turns and forces later tool results into image-analysis framing. The retention logic that governs this is `pruneProcessedHistoryImages` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.ts`), which keeps image blocks from the last `PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` completed turns intact.

`scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-session.ts` drives that real production transform over a realistic multi-turn session and contrasts the pre-fix tool-result shape (base64 image block, as `imageResultFromFile` emitted) with the post-fix shape (text-only, as this PR's catch path emits and as the unit tests below assert). It shows the recent vision-failure image survives history pruning and persists next to later `read` / `browser snapshot` results, while the text-only result leaves zero image blocks so later results stay text-framed.

Reproduce:

```
node --import tsx scripts/repro/browser-vision-failure-session.ts
```

Redacted transcript (content-block types only; no base64 bytes or paths are printed):

```
Repro: configured browser screenshot-vision failure and later tool results (#106703, #105305)
Mechanism: pruneProcessedHistoryImages keeps image blocks from the last 3 completed turns.
The screenshot sits inside that window, so retention alone does not remove a base64 image.

=== PRE-FIX handler output (imageResultFromFile: base64 image block) ===
session turns: 17 messages
prune activated (older images scrubbed): yes
tool results the model sees after prune:
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text,image]
  toolResult(read) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
image blocks persisting in model context: 1

=== POST-FIX handler output (text-only failure result) ===
session turns: 17 messages
prune activated (older images scrubbed): yes
tool results the model sees after prune:
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(read) content-block types: [text]
  toolResult(browser) content-block types: [text]
image blocks persisting in model context: 0

=== verdict ===
PRE-FIX: 1 image block(s) persist next to later read/snapshot results -> session contaminated until /new.
POST-FIX: 0 image block(s) -> later read/browser-snapshot results stay text-framed.

result: PASS
```

The old turn-1 screenshot image is pruned (retention working), yet in the pre-fix run the recent vision-failure image is preserved and rides alongside the later `read` and `browser snapshot` results (`[text,image]`), which is the contamination. In the post-fix run that slot is `[text]` and no image block reaches model context, so later results stay text-framed.

Honesty note on scope: this environment could not run a fully-live browser node plus a real failing vision provider end to end. The repro therefore exercises the real retention transform (`pruneProcessedHistoryImages`) with the two upstream seams represented at their real boundaries: the screenshot tool-result shapes are exactly what the handler emits before/after this change (pre-fix `imageResultFromFile` image block; post-fix text-only, asserted by the tests below), and the later `read` / `browser snapshot` results are ordinary text tool results. The handler-side output shape is independently locked by the tests below and is visible in the diff.

### Handler-side unit and regression tests

Updated and added focused tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts` (these drive the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot path):

- `defangs vision failure fallback text and stays text-only`: vision-failure result is text-only (no `imageResultFromFile`, no image content block, no `details.media`) while preserving the neutralized failure text and share hint.
- `never injects a raw image block when configured vision fails (#106703, #105305)`: configured-vision failure returns zero image content blocks and marks `details.vision.failed`, so the result cannot persist an image across turns.
- No-vision (skipped/unconfigured) path still returns the raw image with sanitization.

Local gate (redacted paths):

```
vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts        98 passed
vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/vision.test.ts        6 passed
vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/history-image-prune.test.ts   12 passed

lint (scripts), format:check, tsgo scripts, tsgo extensions (prod), tsgo extensions (test): green
```

Closes #106703
Related #105305
